title: 8-round AES-192: Eight-round attack: full-key claim

target.description: Reduced 8-round AES-192 with whitening k_-1, final MixColumns omitted, and u_i=MC^-1(k_i). Returns k7 and selected u6, u5 and whitening bytes; the full k7 alone is128 bits of round-key material. Source whole-key claim; the standard schedule permits completing remaining master-key material. A separate completion timing is not itemized.

setting.key_relation: One fixed standard AES schedule; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key subset is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: 2^81 structures of2^32 blocks;2^144 within-structure pairs, tested by early abort and refined key-consistency tables.
assumptions: The four-round one-byte differential is modeled at2^-120; Observation5 enumerates middle states using an average S-box count.
Wrong-key multisets are modeled random. The journal's separate probability proof has documented count/max-probability issues.
Reported time is the online stage; preprocessing is explicit and key-independent. Partial-encryption conversion factors are author estimates.
Key-schedule relations save32 guessed bits including a verified8-bit distant bridge.

time.note: Source online attack cost; dependent on early-abort and wrong-key rejection assumptions.

memory.note: Same special-multiset table as the basic7-round stage.

success.description: No numerical finite-budget success is supplied for this exact key_recovery endpoint. Expected right-pair counts, table coverage and wrong-key rejection are distinct from complete-output success. The existing Observation5 average-to-uniform enumeration conflict remains. Section6 keeps the original inner differential and2^113-data scale. The quoted2^24/2^32 per-pair key suggestions and optimized2^-8 table nonemptiness estimate are intermediate counts/models, not final success. The basic early-abort candidate-reduction point is not a completed attack; the same distinction also applies to selected-subkey and full-key headlines. The full-key author headline does not supply a separately quantified completion probability.

review.scope: Exact19-page proceedings edition; endpoint-event review of Section4.2, Sections5–6 and AppendixA. No probability was added: expected right pairs, conditional enumeration, wrong-key filtering and sampled-table fractions do not quantify this exact output at its recorded data budget. Separate Observation5, time-sign and cost obligations remain unchanged; not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Section4.2 / footnote5 models the original inner four-round one-byte-in/one-byte-out differential at about2^-120 under a random-permutation approximation. This is per eligible pair, not probability of finding a pair, table inclusion, or key recovery.

Sections4.3/6: actual AES192 round-key bytes satisfy the16-bit u6-to-k7 consistency and8-bit whitening-to-k7 identity. This is true-key retention by schedule consistency, conditional on the correct pair/hypothesis, not an independent random-key acceptance or a complete recovery guarantee.
